question: What is the main use of an intradermal injection?
explanation: Intradermal injections place medication into the dermal layer of the skin for local diagnostic reactions, such as allergy or TB tests, rather than for fast absorption into the body. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T6#GNS122_U1_T6_h1)

question: Why is drug absorption very slow after an intradermal injection?

options.A: The medication freezes upon hitting the skin surface
options.B: The dermal layer has very few blood vessels
options.C: Thick subcutaneous fat blocks the medicine pathway
options.D: Large volumes of fluid are injected at once

explanation: The dermis has a limited blood supply, which keeps the medication in place longer instead of quickly entering the bloodstream. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T6#GNS122_U1_T6_h1)

question: Which body site is most commonly used for a routine tuberculin skin test?

options.A: Upper outer quadrant of the buttock

explanation: The inner forearm is easy to reach, has less hair, and makes it easy for the nurse to see and measure any skin reaction. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T6#GNS122_U1_T6_h2)

question: Why must skin layers be targeted precisely during an intradermal injection?

options.A: Epidermal cells will dissolve the needle tip
options.B: Subcutaneous fat inactivates diagnostic agents instantly
options.C: The medicine must stay strictly in the dermal layer
options.D: Muscle movement pushes the drug out too fast

explanation: Placing the fluid outside the dermis can ruin the specific skin response needed for accurate test results like the Mantoux test. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T6#GNS122_U1_T6_h2)

question: What size of syringe is standard for giving an intradermal injection?
explanation: A tuberculin syringe is marked in tiny fractions of a milliliter so you can measure very small doses accurately. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T6#GNS122_U1_T6_h3)

question: Why does a nurse choose a short, thin needle (like a 27-gauge, half-inch) for an intradermal test?

options.A: To force the drug deep into the underlying muscle tissue
options.B: To allow rapid infusion of large volumes of liquid medication
options.C: To prevent the needle from going into the subcutaneous fat
options.D: To reduce the risk of breaking the syringe barrel during use

explanation: Short, fine needles ensure the injection stays shallow in the thin dermal layer of the skin. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T6#GNS122_U1_T6_h3)

question: At what angle should the nurse insert the needle for an intradermal injection?
explanation: A very shallow angle of 5 to 15 degrees keeps the needle tip positioned inside the dermal layer. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T6#GNS122_U1_T6_h4)

question: Why should the nurse avoid massaging the injection site after giving an intradermal test?

options.A: Pressure pushes the needle fragment deeper into the arm
options.B: Friction causes the fragile skin layer to tear easily
options.C: Massage can spread the medication and ruin test results
options.D: Rubbing inactivates the chemical composition of the drug

explanation: Rubbing the small bump (bleb) pushes the medicine into deeper tissue, which changes the local reaction and makes the test invalid. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T6#GNS122_U1_T6_h4)

question: When should the patient return to have a tuberculin skin test read?
explanation: The body's immune response in the skin peaks within this 48-to-72-hour window, making it the correct time to read the result. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T6#GNS122_U1_T6_h5)

question: When checking a positive skin test reaction, what specific physical change does the nurse measure?
explanation: Induration means the area feels hard due to immune cells gathering there. Surface redness alone does not count as a positive reaction. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T6#GNS122_U1_T6_h5)

question: What should the nurse do if a small bump (bleb) does not form during an intradermal injection?

options.A: Withdraw the needle and start over at a new site
options.B: Document the injection as a successful subcutaneous dose
options.C: Apply a hot compress to raise the trapped fluid
options.D: Push more fluid through the syringe to force a bump

explanation: If a bleb does not form, the medication went too deep into the tissue. You need to take the needle out and try again at the correct depth. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T6#GNS122_U1_T6_h6)

question: Which serious emergency is a major concern during skin allergy testing?
explanation: Allergen tests can sometimes trigger a severe, life-threatening allergic reaction across the whole body, so nurses must always be ready to manage emergencies. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T6#GNS122_U1_T6_h6)

question: Which detail is NOT needed when charting an intradermal injection?
explanation: Patient charts only need clinical facts like the drug name, dose, site, date, and time, not personal trivia. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T6#GNS122_U1_T6_h7)

question: Why is it important to teach the patient about returning on time for their tuberculin test reading?

options.A: Local health insurance mandates a physical checkup visit
options.B: The bandage must be professionally removed by the provider
options.C: Results must be read within a specific time window to be valid
options.D: The injection site requires a second booster dose at that time

explanation: If the patient misses the 48-to-72-hour reading window, the test results are no longer accurate and the test must be repeated. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T6#GNS122_U1_T6_h7)
